blocks.tamil_translation: and talking among ourselves. One would cite one Ayah and another would cite another Ayah as proof for his argument. (In this way the dispute in that gathering increased.) Meanwhile the Prophet ﷺ came there; his face appeared red (with anger) as though a pomegranate had been squeezed upon it. Having come, the Prophet ﷺ said, “O people! Were you sent to the world to argue like this? Or have you been commanded to do this? After I leave this world, do not become Kafirs by fighting and cutting off one another's heads” (this action will lead to Kufr).

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ﵄ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: أَنَّ عِيسَي ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ قَالَ: إِنَّمَا اْلأُمُورُ ثَلَاثَةٌ: أَمْرٌ تَبَيَّنَ لَكَ رُشْدُهُ فَاتَّبِعْهُ وَأَمْرٌ تَبَيَّنَ لَكَ غَيُّهُ فَاجْتَنِبْهُ وَأَمْرٌ أُخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ فَرُدَّهُ إِلَي عَالِمِهِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الطبراني في الكبير ورجاله موثقون مجمع الزوائد ٣٩٠/١
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ related what Hazrat Isa (AS) said, “All matters are of three kinds. First, that which is clearly known to you to be the truth; follow it. Second, that which is clearly known to you to be falsehood; keep away from it. Third, that about which it is not clear to you whether it is the right path or the wrong path; ask those who know it (the Ulama) and find out!”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاس ﵄ عَنِ النَّبِيِّﷺ قَالَ: اِتَّقُوا الْحَدِيثَ عَنِّي إِلَّا مَا عَلِمْتُمْ فَمَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَيَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا فَلْيَتَبَوَّاْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَنْ قَالَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ بِرَأْيِهِ فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الترمذي وقال: هذا حديث حسن باب ما جاء في الذي يفسر القران برايه رقم:٢٩٥١
